question.leadin: Eamon de Valera founded this nation's largest political party, Fianna Fail.
question.text: Name this nation, with capital at Dublin. Its northern neighbor is still part of the United Kingdom.
question.clue: Leaders from this country include Eamon de Valera and Patrick Pearse.

swap.leadin: This period of less than ten years caused its country's population to drop by nearly twenty percent.
swap.text: Name this period of disease and starvation caused by infected plants that affected a constituent country of the United Kingdom from 1845 to 1852.
swap.answerHtml: Irish Potato Famine (or Great Famine ; or Great Hunger ; accept Gorta Mor )
swap.clue: Robert Peel repealed the Corn Laws in response to this event, which resulted in certain people converting just to obtain soup.

question.text: Gladstone unsuccessfully pushed for the home rule of this country first conquered by Henry VIII. The failed Easter Rising occurred in this nation, which was also home to the Battle of the Boyne.
question.clue: A civil war erupted in this country between pro and anti-treaty forces led by Michael Collins and Eamon de Valera, respectively.

swap.text: During the crisis of the Third Century Aurelian built a set of these structures around Rome. Antonius Pius and Hadrian each built one of these structures that marked the northern border of the empire.
swap.answerHtml: walls [accept Aurelian Walls; accept Severan Walls; accept Hadrian’s Wall; accept Antonine Wall]
swap.clue: Construction of Austrian towns characterized by this feature rapidly increased in the 11th century.

question.text: The Irish Volunteers, led by Patrick Pearse, joined other rebel groups in this event. Roger Casement was charged with treason after this event.
question.answerHtml: Easter Rising [or Easter Rebellion or Éirí Amach na Cásca; prompt on the Rising or equivalents]
question.clue: Tom Clarke planned this event, and, like Joseph Plunkett and John MacBride, he was executed for taking part.

swap.text: This paramilitary organization tried to assassinate Thatcher in the Brighton Hotel bombing. During her term, a member of this group, Bobby Sands, died from a hunger strike in Maze Prison.
swap.clue: While in H-Block in 1981, a member of this group on hunger strike was elected to parliament.

question.text: This agreement, negotiated in 1998 with the help of Tony Blair, ended the Troubles by effectively dismantling the Provisional IRA.
question.clue: Bertie Ahern and David Andrews were signatories of this document, which was primarily negotiated by David Trimble and John Hume.

swap.leadin: The Annals of the Four Masters describe an event in which unpaid longshoremen in this city refused to help move barrels of gunpowder off of English boats. Shockingly, they exploded.
swap.text: Name this city where Sigtrygg Silkbeard was defeated by the forces of Brian Boru at the Battle of Clontarf. Lord Frederick Cavendish and Thomas Henry Burke were stabbed to death in a park in this city.
swap.clue: This city's King Imar was likely the same person as Ragnar Lodbrok's son Ivar the Boneless.

question.text: In 1873, Parnell displaced the less militant Isaac Butt as leader of the "league" named for this phrase, which was the contemporary name for the goal of Irish autonomists.

swap.text: Forgeries falsely implicated this Irish Nationalist politician in the murders, leading to the downfall of his coalition with the Liberal party. His political career was ultimately undone by his affair with Kitty O'Shea.
swap.clue: One ruler with this name responded to the assassination of his uncle Louis of Orleans by arranging the assassination of the Duke of Burgundy, John the Fearless.

question.text: The collapse of Stormont was precipitated by the resignation of this Sinn Fein politician, who served as Deputy First Minister under the DUP leaders Peter Robinson and Arlene Foster and died shortly after his resignation.

swap.text: Following the Glorious Revolution, William decisively defeated his predecessor, James II, at this battle in Ireland, fought at a namesake river.
swap.clue: The outcome of this battle secured the work of the "Immortal Seven" and is celebrated during the "Glorious Twelfth."

question.leadin: Answer the following about a common act of protest against Britain.
question.text: This man died while leading a ring of Irish republicans on a hunger strike at Maze Prison. His actions were prompted by Britain's decision to revoke the Irish prisoners' Special Category Status.
question.clue: Winston Churchill Boulevard in Tehran was renamed for this man, prompting the British Embassy to move their main address onto a side street.

swap.leadin: About ninety followers of Hugh O'Neill and Rory O'Donnell fled this region for Spain in what was called the "Flight of the Earls."
swap.text: Name this northeastern region of Ireland, which was later heavily settled by Protestant Scots. Its traditional flag features a red hand.
swap.clue: This province was the site of an early 17th century "plantation," in which James I settled thousands of Scots here.

question.leadin: Answer the following about British-Irish conflict.
question.text: Mostly comprised of World War I veterans, this temporary British constabulary unit was loathed for their brutal treatment of Irish civilians, as in the Croke Park massacre.
question.clue: Members of this group were paid just 10 shillings per day, and most were veterans of World War I. This group killed 12 people in Croke Park at a football match in the aftermath of Bloody Sunday.

swap.text: Joseph's elder son, Austen, made his maiden speech in parliament opposing the second Bill proposing this sort of constitutional arrangement for Ireland. John Bright mocked this proposal suggesting that Ireland's catholic majority would make it "Rome Rule."
swap.answerHtml: Irish Home Rule (prompt on “Ireland having its own parliament” or equivalents because the bill itself was unclear)
swap.clue: Edward Carson and James Craig, leaders of the Unionists, campaigned against a 1914 bill aiming to bring about this outcome.

question.text: This younger sister of Charles Parnell led the Ladies' Land League and wrote The Tale of a Great Sham. A plaque on her tombstone carries her quote "the best part of independence; the independence of mind."
question.answerHtml: Anna Catherine Parnell [grudgingly prompt on (A.) Parnell ]

swap.text: A small French army led by Jean Humbert proclaimed the Republic of Connacht after winning the Battle of Castlebar during this uprising, sometimes named for a secret society founded by Wolfe Tone.
swap.answerHtml: Irish Rebellion of 1798 [or United Irishmen Rebellion; accept equivalents mentioning the year 1798; prompt on ‘98]
swap.clue: The losing side of this conflict were defeated at the Battle of Vinegar (+) Hill, and France tacitly provided support for this revolt thanks to the efforts of Wolfe Tone, who died before his planned execution after this event.

question.leadin: Name these sources which document the extreme weather events of 535 to 536 C.E., the most significant global cooling in the past 2,000 years.
question.text: This set of annals documents the frigid weather of the 530s as well as many other severe climate events over centuries of Irish history. These annals were compiled by monks on a namesake island in the Lakes of Killarney.

swap.text: In 1889 Parnell was politically ruined when his affair with this longtime mistress was revealed. Her husband, an Irish MP, filed for divorce and named Parnell as corespondent.
